messages.content:
Diagnosis:
The failing test is verifying the behavior of TypeUtils.isAssignable for various generic List types and arrays of generic List types. This method checks if one generic type is assignable to another, taking into account complex generic constructs like wildcards and bounded types.

Looking at TypeUtils.isAssignable(Type type, Type toType), it delegates to an overloaded method that handles different cases based on the actual runtime type of toType (Class, ParameterizedType, GenericArrayType, WildcardType, TypeVariable).

The critical logic for parameterized types (generic classes/interfaces with type arguments) is in isAssignable(Type type, ParameterizedType toParameterizedType, Map typeVarAssigns). The method:
- Gets the raw class of the target parameterized type.
- Calls getTypeArguments on the source type to get a map from type variables to actual types.
- Calls getTypeArguments on the target parameterized type.
- Then compares each target type argument with the corresponding source argument for assignability, with special handling for wildcards.

The getTypeArguments(Type type, Class<?> toClass, Map subtypeVarAssigns) method is crucial: it extracts all type arguments for a given type (which can be a class, parameterized type, array type, wildcard, or type variable) relative to some target class.

From the lines of getTypeArguments(ParameterizedType parameterizedType, Class<?> toClass, map) method, the logic is:
- If the raw type of the parameterizedType is not assignable to the toClass, return null.
- Otherwise, initialize type argument assignments either from the owner type or from existing assignments.
- Map actual type arguments of the parameterizedType to type variables of the raw class.
- If the toClass is the raw class itself, return the assignments.
- Otherwise, recursively walk up the inheritance chain to gather more type argument assignments.

The current bug report says "TypeUtils.getTypeArguments() misses type arguments for partially-assigned classes." This hints at a problem during the recursive call in getTypeArguments, i.e., when walking up the inheritance hierarchy after mapping current level type variables, the method may be incorrectly mapping or failing to retain proper assignments.

In the failing test, many delegateBooleanAssertion calls are checking assignability of various generic list types with different wildcards, super, extends, and arrays. The test expects some true and some false results.

Likely, getTypeArguments's recursion in the last line:
`return getTypeArguments(getClosestParentType(cls, toClass), toClass, typeVarAssigns);`

may produce incomplete or incorrect mapping of type variables up the hierarchy because it might overwrite typeVarAssigns or fail to merge type variable assignments properly when climbing.

This incomplete or incorrect type variable assignment propagation would cause isAssignable to fail comparison of type arguments in parameterized types, which matches the symptom "misses type arguments for partially-assigned classes."

Hence, the root cause is located in the mechanism of getTypeArguments for ParameterizedType that tries to walk up the class hierarchy and merge type variables but does so incorrectly, missing some bindings or accidentally replacing them.

No recent issue reports contradict or provide additional evidence, so focusing on this method is best.

# Summary: The bug occurs because getTypeArguments when processing a ParameterizedType does not properly propagate and merge type variables assignments for partially-parameterized types while walking the inheritance chain, causing isAssignable to incorrectly return false for some valid assignments checked in the failing test.

Recommended methods for fix: 
- org.apache.commons.lang3.reflect.TypeUtils.getTypeArguments(java.lang.reflect.ParameterizedType, java.lang.Class<?>, java.util.Map<java.lang.reflect.TypeVariable<?>, java.lang.reflect.Type>)
- org.apache.commons.lang3.reflect.TypeUtils.isAssignable(java.lang.reflect.Type, java.lang.reflect.ParameterizedType, java.util.Map<java.lang.reflect.TypeVariable<?>, java.lang.reflect.Type>)

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
